article_title: The personalization paradox: how AI-driven adaptive learning environments are associated with college students'
citation: Li J, Lin Z and Qiu C (2026) The personalization paradox: how AI-driven adaptive learning environments are associated with college students' academic emotions and self-regulation learning—a moderated mediation model. Front. Psychol. 17:1915839. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1915839
title: Integrated CVT–SRL moderated mediation model of the personalization paradox
description: The article integrates control-value theory (Pekrun, 2006) with self-regulated learning theory (Zimmerman, 2000) in a single moderated mediation structure: AI-adaptive environment → academic emotions (enjoyment, anxiety, boredom) → SRL, with AI literacy moderating the first stage. As the authors state, "CVT clarifies why adaptive environments foster emotional responses by altered control-value appraisals; SRL theory demonstrates how these emotional states translates into weakened self-regulatory actions." The model frames the personalization paradox as operating through affective pathways rather than purely cognitive ones.
requirements: Temporal separation of measurement waves to capture progressive change in the constructs
constraints: The article states the observational design precludes final causal inference
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning
academic emotion regulation in AI-mediated learning
examples: The study tested the model with a three-wave longitudinal survey (T1 environment and AI literacy, T2 emotions, T3 SRL) across one semester
key_sources: Li J, Lin Z and Qiu C (2026) The personalization paradox: how AI-driven adaptive learning environments are associated with college students' academic emotions and self-regulation learning—a moderated mediation model. Front. Psychol. 17:1915839. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1915839

article_title: Multidimensional perceived school support and AI learning anxiety among university students: the mediating roles of control-value appraisals
citation: Jiang H, Chen B and Chen Q (2026). Multidimensional perceived school support and AI learning anxiety among university students: the mediating roles of control-value appraisals. Front. Psychol. 17:1951992. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951992
title: Control-value theory integrated with social support theory and TAM as an account of AI learning anxiety
description: The article proposes an integrated framework in which control-value theory is the principal account of AI learning anxiety: "achievement emotions reﬂect learners' judgments of how much control they have over activities and outcomes and how much value they place on them". AI learning self-efficacy operationalizes perceived control, and AI perceived usefulness (from TAM) operationalizes value. Social support theory supplies the three dimensions of perceived school support (emotional, informational, instrumental), specified as a distal contextual correlate of students' immediate appraisals. The model was tested with SEM in a sample of Chinese undergraduates.
requirements: Requires measurement of perceived school support, AI learning self-efficacy, AI perceived usefulness, and AI learning anxiety as distinct constructs
constraints: The article states the sequential ordering reflects the proposed structural model rather than an empirically established temporal process, and the design cannot establish causal mediation
target_learners: university undergraduates using AI tools in their learning
target_learning_goals: emotional adjustment to AI-supported learning, including reduced AI learning anxiety and informed judgments of AI's educational value
examples: The structural model specified PSS as a second-order construct with paths to ASE, APU, and ALA, and sequential mediation through self-efficacy then perceived usefulness.
key_sources: Jiang H, Chen B and Chen Q (2026). Multidimensional perceived school support and AI learning anxiety among university students: the mediating roles of control-value appraisals. Front. Psychol. 17:1951992. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951992

article_title: Bridging Research and Practice: A Cognitively Based Classroom Intervention for Teaching Experimentation Skills to Elementary School Children
citation: Eva Erdosne Toth, David Klahr, and Zhe Chen. (2000). Bridging Research and Practice: A Cognitively Based Classroom Intervention for Teaching Experimentation Skills to Elementary School Children. Cognition and Instruction, 18(4), 423–459. https://doi.org/10.1207/S1532690XCI1804_2
title: Benchmark lesson: a classroom CVS unit translating the laboratory training procedure
description: The benchmark lesson is a classroom instructional unit that translates the laboratory CVS training procedure into a fourth-grade science lesson using the ramps materials. It consists of exploratory group experiments, about 20 minutes of whole-class expository instruction following five teacher steps (initiate reflective discussion on a bad comparison, model correct thinking, test understanding, reinforce correct thinking, summarize rationale), and application experiments. The authors "attempted to engineer a classroom learning environment (Brown, 1992) that students could refer to during future hands-on activities calling for the design of informative experiments."
requirements: A regular classroom teacher to deliver the expository instruction; students work in groups of 3 to 5 with their own ramp materials and preformatted worksheets for recording setups and outcomes
constraints: Only the ramps domain was used during classroom work (springs and sinking were used in interviews); the lesson is a one-time event focusing on a procedural skill rather than repeated cycles; the teacher did not provide corrective feedback on CVS during exploration or application phases
target_learning_goals: designing unconfounded (controlled) experiments using the control of variables strategy
justifying and evaluating experimental designs
examples: Teachers led a short demonstration of ramp setups, a 5-minute domain knowledge pretest, four exploratory group experiments, roughly 20 minutes of whole-class expository instruction, and four application experiments, with students individually recording setups and certainty on worksheets
key_sources: Eva Erdosne Toth, David Klahr, and Zhe Chen. (2000). Bridging Research and Practice: A Cognitively Based Classroom Intervention for Teaching Experimentation Skills to Elementary School Children. Cognition and Instruction, 18(4), 423–459. https://doi.org/10.1207/s1532690xci1804_1

article_title: How gaze and proxemics shape and signal shared regulatory processes during AI-supported collaborative learning
citation: Ridwan Whitehead · Andy Nguyen · Sanna Järvelä. (2026). How gaze and proxemics shape and signal shared regulatory processes during AI-supported collaborative learning. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-026-09478-7
title: Automated computer-vision pipeline for extracting gaze and proxemics from ordinary 2D classroom video
description: The study adapted the Sharingan gaze-estimation framework (Tafasca et al., 2024), a pretrained transformer-based model reported with AUC 0.944, to derive joint attention and mutual gaze frame by frame from standard 2D video. A separate pipeline combining YOLOv11 pose estimation, DeepOCSort tracking, and depth-based distance computation computed pairwise interpersonal distances, categorized via 33rd/66th percentile thresholds into close, neutral, and far levels. The authors present this as a nonintrusive, scalable methodological alternative to intrusive sensors, lab-only setups, and manual coding in authentic classrooms.
requirements: RGB and depth video pairs synchronized; camera geometry calibration for depth-weighted distance computation
constraints: Parameters kept constant across groups given similar camera placement; relative (percentile-based) distance categorization used because seating configurations varied across groups
target_learners: secondary school students in face-to-face collaborative group work
target_learning_goals: automated measurement of nonverbal coordination cues during collaborative learning
examples: Gaze extraction used a YOLOv5-based head detector with OCSORT tracking and the Sharingan transformer model; joint attention required predicted gaze points within 125 pixels, and mutual gaze required reciprocal gaze points within each other's head bounding box
key_sources: Ridwan Whitehead · Andy Nguyen · Sanna Järvelä. (2026). How gaze and proxemics shape and signal shared regulatory processes during AI-supported collaborative learning. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-026-09478-7

article_title: Classroom emotions in civic education: A multilevel approach to antecedents and effects
citation: Graf, E., Stempfer, L., Muis, K. R., & Goetz, T. (2023). Classroom emotions in civic education: A multilevel approach to antecedents and effects. Draft version 1.0, University of Vienna / McGill University (not peer-reviewed preprint).
title: Control-value theory applied to civic education: classroom context as distal antecedent and valence/arousal-categorized emotions as mediators of civic learning
description: The study applies Pekrun's control-value theory, in which "the classroom context is an important factor in determining the experience of classroom emotions," and emotions are categorized by valence (positive/negative) and arousal (activating/deactivating). Distal environmental antecedents such as classroom climate shape emotions, which in turn relate to learning processes and outcomes and can mediate between context and outcomes. The article reports that results "strongly support the theoretical assumptions of the control-value theory" in the civic education domain.
requirements: Emotions are measured as discrete class-related emotions (enjoyment, shame, anxiety, boredom) distinguished by valence and activation
constraints: Tested in civic education with vocational-school students in Austria; observational and cross-sectional, so causal claims are not supported
target_learning_goals: political knowledge
intended political participation
examples: The study tested CVT hypotheses with doubly-latent multilevel SEM on survey and knowledge-test data from 1,117 students
key_sources: Graf, E., Stempfer, L., Muis, K. R., & Goetz, T. (2023). Classroom emotions in civic education: A multilevel approach to antecedents and effects. Draft version 1.0, University of Vienna / McGill University (not peer-reviewed preprint). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2023.101869

article_title: Physiological synchrony amongst medical residents during crisis management simulation training and a video-based assessment of leaders’ performance
citation: Lucia Patino Melo, Sebastian Wallot, Keerat Grewal, Matthew Moreno, Osamu Nomura, Jason M. Harley. (2026). Physiological synchrony amongst medical residents during crisis management simulation training and a video-based assessment of leaders' performance. Learning and Instruction 102 (2026) 102302. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102302
title: Control-Value Theory of Achievement Emotions as a framework for interpreting physiological arousal in simulation
description: The study draws on the Control-Value Theory of Achievement Emotions (CVT) to operationalize and interpret EDA as an emotional expression component. CVT treats emotional arousal as a key dimension of emotion alongside valence and object focus, and holds that "the learner's perceived control over the learning situation and the value the learner places on the learning situation" are antecedents of emotions. The authors use CVT to hypothesize that residents' high value appraisals and uncertain control appraisals arouse emotions like anxiety, and that shared goals (saving the patient) produce parallel appraisal changes that become visible as physiological synchrony. They caution that valence and object focus were not measured, so claims about discrete emotions require caution.
requirements: Interpretation of EDA as emotional arousal requires acknowledging which emotional dimensions (valence, object focus) are not measured
constraints: Appraisals were inferred from context rather than measured; the article states claims about valence and discrete emotions require caution
target_learners: medical residents in crisis resource management simulation training
target_learning_goals: understanding and managing emotional arousal during team-based crisis management practice
examples: The authors hypothesize residents' appraisals of control decline when the simulated patient deteriorates, producing shared arousal visible in EDA synchrony
key_sources: Lucia Patino Melo, Sebastian Wallot, Keerat Grewal, Matthew Moreno, Osamu Nomura, Jason M. Harley. (2026). Physiological synchrony amongst medical residents during crisis management simulation training and a video-based assessment of leaders' performance. Learning and Instruction 102 (2026) 102302. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102302

article_title: A sequence of learning processes in an intelligent tutoring system from topic-related appraisals to learning gains
citation: Chevalère, J., Yun, H. S., Henke, A., Pinkwart, N., Hafner, V., & Lazarides, R. (2023). A sequence of learning processes in an intelligent tutoring system from topic-related appraisals to learning gains. Learning and Instruction, 87, 101799. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2023.101799
title: Control-value theory sequence applied to ITS learning: partial correlational support but difficult causal establishment
description: The article tests Pekrun's control-value theory (CVT), which posits a sequence from topic-related cognitive appraisals of control and value, through activity-related emotions (enjoyment, boredom), to engagement, task performance, and learning gains, including reciprocal feedback loops. In the ITS context the authors found "partial support for the application of CVT to the ITS context on a correlational basis", while "causation was more difficult to establish due to the influence of multiple confounders challenging the expected unidirectional and reciprocal relations". The theory served as the framework for hypotheses and a three-step path-analytic testing procedure.
requirements: Measurement of appraisals, emotions, engagement, performance, and knowledge at temporally ordered phases (pretest, test, posttest) as in the study's three-day protocol
constraints: The article states the difficulty of establishing sequential causation in the current ITS context due to confounders
Multilevel analyses were not performed due to the small number of schools (N = 5) and classrooms (N = 11)
target_learning_goals: Science learning (climate change knowledge) in an open-ended ITS environment
examples: Path analyses of 140 students' data across pretest, four one-hour Betty's Brain sessions, and posttest
key_sources: Chevalère, J., Yun, H. S., Henke, A., Pinkwart, N., Hafner, V., & Lazarides, R. (2023). A sequence of learning processes in an intelligent tutoring system from topic-related appraisals to learning gains. Learning and Instruction, 87, 101799. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2023.101799

article_title: Pragmatic AI in education and its role in mathematics learning and teaching
citation: Gabriel, F., Kennedy, J.P., Marrone, R. & Leonard, S. (2025). Pragmatic AI in education and its role in mathematics learning and teaching. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00315-4
title: Control-Value Theory account of mathematics anxiety in learning mathematics
description: The article adopts the Control-Value Theory of Achievement Emotions as its explanatory account of maths anxiety: "anxiety in educational contexts can be understood as the feeling that arises when students place value on a subject like mathematics but perceive a lack of control over their performance in it". It uses this account to structure a conceptual model in which students' appraisals of control and value shape emotional responses and likelihood of success, and to justify individually tailored, relative measurement of these appraisals over time.
requirements: Recognition that appraisals of control and value vary significantly across individuals and situations, implying relative rather than absolute measurement
constraints: The authors state the accompanying model is not a complete representation of the process of learning and forms one sub-system in a larger process
target_learners: School students learning mathematics, including middle school students
target_learning_goals: Reducing mathematics anxiety
Supporting socio-emotional learning in mathematics
examples: The article applies the account in Figure 1, where appraisals of control and value feed success in mathematics activities and maths anxiety
key_sources: Gabriel, F., Kennedy, J.P., Marrone, R. & Leonard, S. (2025). Pragmatic AI in education and its role in mathematics learning and teaching. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00315-4

article_title: The impact of teacher-student relationship quality on achievement emotions in English as a foreign language within a Confucian heritage cultural context: an examination of the mediating roles of cognitive appraisals.
citation: Wu Qiong. (2026). The impact of teacher-student relationship quality on achievement emotions in English as a foreign language within a Confucian heritage cultural context: an examination of the mediating roles of cognitive appraisals. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04561-y
title: Control-value theory extended with TSRQ as a distal social-contextual antecedent of achievement emotions
description: The article applies control-value theory (CVT), in which "learners' control appraisals and value appraisals are proposed as proximal antecedents of achievement emotions, whereas contextual and personal factors are conceptualized as distal antecedents that influence emotions indirectly through these appraisals." It positions TSRQ as one such distal, appraisal-relevant contextual factor offering "feedback, expectations, and emotional safety cues" that students use to judge competence and task value. The hypothesized "TSRQ → control/value appraisals → achievement emotions" model was tested among Chinese college EFL learners in a Confucian heritage cultural context.
requirements: Learners must perceive their relationships with teachers as sources of information about their competence and the value of learning tasks.
constraints: The model was tested cross-sectionally in a single Chinese teachers' college, and CHC orientation or cultural values were not measured as an operationalized explanatory variable.
target_learning_goals: achievement emotions in foreign language learning
key_sources: Wu Qiong. (2026). The impact of teacher-student relationship quality on achievement emotions in English as a foreign language within a Confucian heritage cultural context: an examination of the mediating roles of cognitive appraisals. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04561-y

article_title: Unpacking grit in exam-oriented education: divergent roles of perseverance and consistency in foreign language achievement.
citation: Weng Tsung-han and Peng Jinchang. (2026). Unpacking grit in exam-oriented education: divergent roles of perseverance and consistency in foreign language achievement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04312-z
title: Contextual refinement of Control-Value Theory: the emotional consequences of value depend on its regulatory quality and the environment's autonomy affordances
description: The article refines Control-Value Theory for high-stakes contexts. CVT posits that stable value appraisals foster enjoyment when accompanied by perceived control, but the study shows "the emotional consequences of value depend not only on its stability but on its regulatory quality". In exam-oriented systems, stable goal commitment indexed by COI may reflect introjected or externally regulated motivation, so value appraisals may coexist with boredom rather than produce enjoyment. The authors frame this as "a contextual refinement rather than a rejection of CVT", specifying boundary conditions and supporting a broader shift toward integrating trait-based models with ecological analysis of institutional structures.
requirements: Application requires attending to the motivational source of value (autonomous vs. controlled) and the autonomy-supportive affordances of the learning environment.
constraints: The authors state the maladaptive COI pathway was observed within a high-stakes, summative assessment system with competitive selection and limited curricular flexibility, and should not be generalized beyond it.
target_learners: Senior high school students in high-stakes exam-oriented systems
target_learning_goals: Understanding how achievement emotions (enjoyment, boredom) transmit trait effects to foreign language achievement
examples: The study situates CVT within the Gaokao-centered Chinese EFL environment, showing value appraisals under external framing may coexist with boredom.
key_sources: Weng Tsung-han and Peng Jinchang. (2026). Unpacking grit in exam-oriented education: divergent roles of perseverance and consistency in foreign language achievement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04312-z

article_title: Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement.
citation: Wu Yajun, Kang Xia, Li Yiyan. (2025). Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03685-x
title: Control-value-theory-based chain mediation model: PsyCap → academic boredom → behavioural engagement → academic achievement
description: The article constructs, grounded in control-value theory, an integrated serial mediation model in which "PsyCap → academic boredom → behavioural engagement → academic achievement". CVT holds that distal factors such as PsyCap influence achievement emotions, and that achievement emotions affect achievement through engagement. The study claims to be the first to integrate the antecedents and consequences of achievement emotions in a single model within the EFL context, validated with SEM in 1460 Chinese secondary EFL learners.
requirements: All variables measured within the domain-specific EFL context
Control of socio-demographic covariates (gender, age, SES) in SEM analyses
constraints: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference, as the authors state
Developed and validated within a Confucian heritage culture context
target_learners: Secondary EFL learners aged 12-17 in China
target_learning_goals: EFL achievement
Reduction of academic boredom
Behavioural engagement in English learning
examples: The structural model achieved good fit (CFI = 0.945, TLI = 0.938, RMSEA = 0.048, SRMR = 0.038)
key_sources: Wu Yajun, Kang Xia, Li Yiyan. (2025). Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03685-x

article_title: Profiles of control, value and achievement emotions in primary school mathematics lessons.
citation: Symes, W., Lichtenfeld, S., Wood, P., & Putwain, D. W. (2025). Profiles of control, value and achievement emotions in primary school mathematics lessons. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 95, 888–902. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12768
title: Control-value theory profiles of appraisals and achievement emotions in mathematics lessons
description: Control-value theory (CVT; Pekrun, 2006) holds that achievement emotions arise from combinations of control and value appraisals. The article operationalizes this as theoretically plausible profiles (Table 1) in which, for example, "enjoyment should arise from high control and high value, boredom from either high or low control and low perceived value, and anxiety from high value but low control". The study tested these profiles person-centredly in primary-school mathematics, identifying Positive, Mixed and Negative profiles that broadly matched the theorized combinations, providing what the authors call a robust test of CVT in this context.
requirements: Profiles require measures of control, value (intrinsic, attainment, utility) and the emotions enjoyment, boredom and anxiety from the same students
constraints: The article notes appraisals may not always be temporal antecedents of emotions, since in familiar contexts emotions may become habitualized and appraisals and emotions are assumed to be reciprocal
target_learners: Primary school students (year 5, age ~9) in mathematics lessons
target_learning_goals: Mathematics achievement and affective experiences of learning mathematics
examples: The study measured control (α = .82), three value subscales and enjoyment, boredom and anxiety (AEQ-ES) at T2, and identified profiles matching the theorized Positive and Mixed patterns
key_sources: Symes, W., Lichtenfeld, S., Wood, P., & Putwain, D. W. (2025). Profiles of control, value and achievement emotions in primary school mathematics lessons. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 95, 888–902. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12768

article_title: Outcome-based simulation training for ultrasound-guided central venous catheter placement: clinical impact on preventing mechanical complications.
citation: Tokumine Joho, Yorozu Tomoko, Moriyama Kiyoshi, Suzuki Teruko, Okada Chikako. (2025). Outcome-based simulation training for ultrasound-guided central venous catheter placement: clinical impact on preventing mechanical complications. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06739-1
title: Technical certification skill test for ultrasound-guided central venous catheter placement scoring needle visibility, hand–eye coordination, and avoidance of posterior wall penetration
description: A mandatory skill test launched in 2016 for junior and newly hired senior residents before clinical central venous catheter placement, based on the Japanese Association for Medical Simulation's Instructors' Guide Ver. 5. It evaluates "needle tip visualization", "hand–eye coordination", and "the avoidance of posterior wall penetration of the vein", with a minimum score of 3 required to pass; failed trainees receive examiner feedback and may retake the test until passing.
requirements: Trainees first watch a committee-created video and train independently in the Clinical Simulation Lab with a simulator, ultrasound machine, and central venous catheter set before testing.
constraints: Previously, preclinical testing focused only on procedural flow, not technical certification; the test criteria remained unchanged even as training shifted from the tilting technique to the sliding technique.
target_learning_goals: ultrasound-guided internal jugular venipuncture technique
avoidance of posterior vein wall penetration
examples: Examiners explained which specific aspects needed improvement after failure, and trainees retook the test until they successfully passed.
key_sources: Tokumine Joho, Yorozu Tomoko, Moriyama Kiyoshi, Suzuki Teruko, Okada Chikako. (2025). Outcome-based simulation training for ultrasound-guided central venous catheter placement: clinical impact on preventing mechanical complications. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06739-1
